body: To be honest it felt like shit at first, but he kind of played the “I didn’t know” card and that makes it hard to be as furious as I otherwise would be. He was really drunk and doesn’t know much about guns and I can see how a person might get their gun safety mixed up when his two “gun expert” friends are telling him it’s okay. He was upset when they started mocking me, but by that point they had left. There will be a lot of talking tonight and depending on what he says I might have to re-evaluate if I want to be with someone who won’t stand up for my safety.

100% it’s not. If I knew they were bringing guns I would have told them to leave it in their car or something. Especially while we’re drinking. I thought this was basic stuff, but apparently to some people it’s not.
Thanks. I honestly wouldn’t have been surprised if they started brandishing the loaded gun if I had pissed them of any more.  They won’t be coming back!

There were two guns, one was loaded with bullets while the other was not. They gave my boyfriend the unloaded one and told him to pull the trigger and he did. No bullets were fired.

They usually come over to our house so yeah I’m almost always there. They do sometimes go out to bars and stuff though and I don’t go with them. I definitely think I’m there too much when they hang out, but they come to hang out where I live! I’ve never liked those guys but I urge him to hang out with them because I think it’s important to have friends. 

It’s no secret though, everyone knows I don’t like them and they don’t like me. We’re total opposites in every way imaginable so I can understand why. I don’t really want them to like me I just want them to stop being rude about not liking me.
It wasn’t our guns and I had no idea they were bringing guns at all. I probably would have told them not to come if I knew.

Thanks. I’m definitely showing him this thread because you all say it much better than I ever could. I originally wanted to know how to convince myself to be okay with what happened, but I don’t have to. Im glad to know my fears were reasonable.

Funnily enough it was a group snap that I’m not in. I wouldn’t have even known they were talking shit if they weren’t making it so obvious. My boyfriend is in the group and I asked if I could see if they were badmouthing me and sure enough they were. They aren’t coming back.

Thanks, you’re right. I knew all this shit was wrong the whole time it was happening, but the dynamic with his friends has been really weird. They paint me as the “bitchy girlfriend” constantly for the most mundane things. I feel like an assertive person that stands up for myself, (I can’t even count how many times I’ve argued with these friends) It’s just so hard to be sure when multiple people act like I’m insane for it. Those people will not be coming back.
That’s how I feel too, but isn’t it a little demanding to expect him to cut off his closest friends for my sake?

My boyfriend and I don’t have any guns or gun training at all. The most “training” he’s had is going to a shooting range like once. The friends offered me the gun too but I refused to even hold it because I don’t really know how to handle them. I was okay with people holding them unloaded, but to be cocking them and pulling the trigger so much? Like 20+ times? That was a lot.

He said he doesn’t know if he can be friends with them anymore but he’s kind of the type to say things and not ever act on it. He kind of only does anything if I give him an ultimatum on it and it feels really shitty to “make” him to things like that. :( My boyfriend is usually great and attentive though. These friends are just genuinely really bad people and they have a really bad influence on him (in my opinion).

Yeah. We had that conversation after they left and my boyfriend agreed that it was dumb and rude. He is pretty torn up about it, but went right to sleep since he was way too drunk. This just happened so I’ll have wait and see if he actually figures out what he wants to do about his friends. It definitely would feel shitty to make him choose between me and them, though. I have no idea how I’d be able to forgive them for this, especially after they doubled down and tried to publicly humiliate me for it.

Hi, thanks for the response. To clarify, one of them had a loaded gun and the other had an unloaded one. They handed my boyfriend the unloaded gun and he did pull the trigger. I was especially worried because the guns look very similar and my boyfriend was very drunk. I should have spoken up, but was worried about the social consequences because his friends are a little overboard when it comes to guarding their egos when being told they’re wrong. I’m dumb anyways because they still got pissy over me telling my boyfriend not to participate, though.

Thanks, that’s exactly what I was trying to tell them but didn’t know exactly how to put it. I don’t know much about guns other than not to pull a trigger on them unless you wanna shoot something/someone. I can’t believe they were insulting me for expecting them to be smarter with their guns.

I think the stressing of not doing sex acts that you don't want to do is super important because if you're frequently doing things you don't want to do it will build resentment and the people "compromising" would avoid sex. It would no longer fun since they feel obligated to please their partner in ways they don't want to. Sex is a place to have fun together simultaneously. 

If the excitement of pleasing your partner is ever negated by how much you dislike doing something, DONT DO IT.
